skill.title: Establish uniform deformation rings before shaping a smooth profile
preconditions: the target surface is intended to deform as one continuous smooth form
the local topology can support a traversable quad ring
the current ticket identifies the affected region and supplies a valid loop-cut target/parameters
required_observations: ring spacing along the deformation axis
base-cage quad aspect ratios in the affected region
profile or silhouette deviation before and after shaping
evaluated surface for buckling, pinching, and manifoldness
action_policy: Establish the full primary extent first, then distribute enough rings uniformly before applying proportional, lattice, or similar broad deformation.
Use only enough rings to represent the curvature and output scale; the transfer used 13 axial rings and 12 radial vertices, not a blanket high-density mesh.

After the uniform base is established, move rings to match the target profile where the reference demands non-uniform curvature; uniform setup is a controllable starting distribution, not a ban on purposeful local density.
Do not apply this hint when the surface is intentionally stepped, the ring path is interrupted by poles/triangles, or a ticket has not localized a valid loop-cut target.
expected_effects: lower profile approximation error for the same ring count when the alternative contains accumulated manual-step spacing/radius error
more even side-quad aspect ratios before deformation
a smoother and more controllable evaluated highlight flow
failure_predicates: the new ring does not traverse the intended quad region
added density creates pinching or unnecessary complexity without measurable silhouette improvement
another relevant view or surface channel regresses
recovery: reject or rollback the scoped loop-cut decision
use a local reroute, lattice, curve/profile construction, or fewer purposefully placed rings when uniform rings are not suitable

planner_hint.reason: The transferred experiment showed that uniform pre-distribution materially improved profile accuracy and quad density at the same topology budget.
planner_hint.expected_effect: Create a controllable, evenly distributed ring scaffold before the scoped smooth deformation.
verification: confirm the loop traversed the intended quad ring only
measure ring spacing and affected-region quad aspect ratios
reapply or preview the deformation and compare the profile/silhouette
inspect the evaluated surface and all relevant views for regression

sources.description: Blender Guru deliberately demonstrates uneven manual extrude-and-scale spacing, then establishes the full height and adds uniformly spaced loop cuts before proportional deformation.

The source lesson was independently spot-checked in the in-app browser and replayed through the committed Gemini video-understanding pipeline; the transfer claim remains grounded in the older tighter timestamp study rather than the generated source metadata.

experiments.limitations: The negative control deliberately encodes uneven spacing and small deterministic manual radius errors. The result validates the tutorial's demonstrated failure mode on one radial product form; it does not prove that every manually stepped mesh is inferior or that all deformations require uniform density.

skill.version_scope: Blender 5.2 LTS transfer; source tutorial used Blender 2.78.5 UI
skill.status_note: A predeclared different-shape transfer passed both the modeling lab and an independent fresh-process verifier. The skill is planner-actionable only for matching localized tickets with scene-owned operation parameters; no real held-out asset runtime use has occurred yet.

skill.title: New material added via data.materials.append() renders unused because faces still point at the old slot index
skill.problem: Calling obj.data.materials.append(new_mat) adds a new slot but does NOT reassign any polygon's material_index to point at it. If slot 0 already existed (e.g. empty/null from object creation) and the new material became slot 1, every face keeps material_index=0, so the newly 'assigned' material renders on zero faces even though it appears in the material list.
skill.symptom: obj.data.materials shows the expected material name(s), but sorted(set(p.material_index for p in obj.data.polygons)) == [0] where slot 0 is null or a different material -- the intended material is present but structurally orphaned.

fix.summary: After appending a material, explicitly set polygon.material_index to the new slot's index for the faces that should use it (usually all faces for a single-material object), then remove any now-empty slots.
bpy_bmesh_steps: for p in obj.data.polygons: p.material_index = target_slot_index
fix.code_snippet: verified directly against Bottle and Flashlight in runs/2026-08-07_decision-cycles/ (decisions 040-042)

evidence.note: bpy.ops.object.material_slot_remove_unused() reported 'Removed 1 slots' without fixing the actual defect -- verify with a direct polygon.material_index scan, don't trust the operator's own report

skill.applicability: Any time a material is programmatically assigned via data.materials.append() (or a material appears unassigned/unused after seeming to be set), check polygon.material_index distribution before trusting that shading is correct.

runtime_usage.problem: Accent material existed in slot 1 but no polygon used it
runtime_usage.action: Assign the intended top-half polygons to material slot 1

skill.title: Setting material.diffuse_color does not affect the actual rendered Base Color on a node-based Principled BSDF material
skill.problem: material.diffuse_color is a legacy/display property. When use_nodes=True (the default for materials created via bpy.data.materials.new()), the actual rendered appearance comes from the node graph -- specifically the Principled BSDF's 'Base Color' input socket -- which defaults to gray [0.8,0.8,0.8,1.0] and is NOT automatically synced from diffuse_color.
skill.symptom: Code sets mat.diffuse_color = (r,g,b,1.0) and it appears to succeed (no error, the property reads back correctly), but the object renders/displays as flat default gray. Comparing bsdf.inputs['Base Color'].default_value against mat.diffuse_color reveals they differ.

fix.summary: Set the BSDF node's Base Color input directly, not (or in addition to) diffuse_color.
bpy_bmesh_steps: bsdf = next(n for n in mat.node_tree.nodes if n.type == 'BSDF_PRINCIPLED')
fix.code_snippet: verified directly on Bottle_Mat_v2, Flashlight_Mat_v2, SimpleBlock_Mat in runs/2026-08-07_decision-cycles/ (decisions 076-079)

evidence.note: found by comparing the two properties directly, not by visual inspection -- the bug was silent, no error, no warning

skill.applicability: Any time a material's color needs to be set programmatically on a node-based material (use_nodes=True), verify the BSDF's actual input sockets, not just diffuse_color -- especially since assigning diffuse_color silently succeeds with no indication the render output is unaffected.

applicability.surface: any (rim/transition where two regions of a control cage meet at different subdivision resolutions)
applicability.defect: n-gons at a resolution-mismatch boundary between a more-subdivided region and its unsubdivided neighbor

preconditions: control cage feeds a Subdivision Surface modifier (Catmull-Clark)
one region was subdivided (e.g. subdivide_selection) without matching the surrounding, unsubdivided faces' shared boundary edges
the mismatch produced n-gons on the neighboring faces (observed: 7-sided, from 5 verts along the new-resolution shared edge + 2 original corners)
required_observations: evaluated_probe.evaluated_surface_quality (area_outlier_count, max_adjacent_face_angle_radians) before and after the fix
evaluated_probe.evaluated_valence_distribution -- specifically whether new poles cluster at the boundary/transition or stay confined to pre-existing corners
action_policy: Prefer re-topologizing the boundary so both sides share matching edge resolution (an all-quad grid across the transition), over the faster fix of triangulate_ngons on the mismatched faces, even when the affected region is currently flat (the condition under which triangulate_ngons was judged 'low risk' in the moment this was found).

This is stated by the human as a general quad-hygiene preference for subdivision control cages, not a claim specific to this one transition -- do not narrow the applicability to 'only curved transitions' or 'only where pinching is visually obvious' without separate evidence for that boundary.
expected_effects: no new poles introduced at the resolution-mismatch boundary itself
evaluated surface shows no area-outlier cluster at the boundary
moderate, not extreme, max adjacent-face angle across the transition
success_predicates: evaluated_valence_distribution's non-4 poles are all traceable to pre-existing geometry (e.g. original box corners), none newly introduced at the boundary
failure_predicates: new valence-3/5 poles appear clustered at the boundary after the fix
recovery: if the all-quad re-topology itself introduces new clustered poles at the boundary, that is real evidence AGAINST blanket-applying this preference at that specific geometry, not a reason to fall back to triangulation by default -- re-inspect and treat as a new, separate problem

sources.description: User directly re-topologized the SoapDish rim by hand in the Blender GUI (live external edit, detected via check_external_edit), replacing an agent-applied triangulate_ngons fix with a resolution-matched all-quad grid.
sources.stated_reasoning: General quad hygiene in subdivision control cages -- not specifically about pole placement at this transition. Given directly when asked, after the fact, per directive section 46 ('human corrections are evidence, not automatically truth -- form a hypothesis').
sources.trust_tier: not applicable (Tier A-D is for external research sources; this is a direct, first-party correction from the project's own user, treated as real evidence in its own right, distinct from and not to be confused with a Tier-A/B external source)

experiments.description: Measured the evaluated mesh AFTER the human's fix (258v/512e/256f, valence {3: 8, 4: 250}, area_outlier_count 0, max_adjacent_face_angle_radians 0.802). Did NOT measure the evaluated quality of the original agent triangulate_ngons fix before it was overwritten by the live edit -- there is no direct A/B comparison, only the post-fix result plus the general knowledge (Blender Manual, general SubD theory) that triangles under Catmull-Clark can produce different curvature behavior than quads.
experiments.limitation: No controlled minimal-scene experiment (directive section 41 style: variant A/B/C on a throwaway mesh) has been run yet to isolate whether the SPECIFIC improvement here came from 'quads vs triangles' or from 'matched vs mismatched resolution' -- these were changed together in the human's single fix, not independently.

skill.status_note: Not EXPERIMENTALLY_TESTED: evidence is one real observational data point from a live human correction plus post-fix measurement, not an isolated controlled experiment. Promote to EXPERIMENTALLY_TESTED only after a dedicated minimal-scene test separating the 'quads vs triangles' variable from the 'matched vs mismatched resolution' variable, per directive section 41.

applicability.defect: non-manifold geometry or a no-op modifier caused by incorrect stack order

preconditions: a modifier stack combines Mirror with Subdivision Surface, or Solidify with Bevel, or Boolean with Bevel, or Mirror with Bevel
the mesh has an open boundary that Mirror welds (Mirror+Subdivision, Mirror+Bevel), or is a flat/open shell that Solidify gives thickness to (Solidify+Bevel)
required_observations: evaluated vertex positions near the mirror seam, to distinguish a genuinely flat/continuous seam from a carved/rounded one
evaluated vertex/face count, to detect a modifier silently doing nothing (e.g. Bevel on an unsolidified plane)
action_policy: For Mirror plus Subdivision Surface, test both candidate orders on the actual seam topology. Subdivision-before-Mirror repaired the original flat-seam failure, but a later exact-seam half-cylinder stayed manifold in both orders; do not promote one shape's result into a universal order rule.

Bevel should be placed BEFORE Mirror when a seamless join across the mirror plane is wanted. Mirror-before-Bevel causes Bevel to treat the former seam edges as ordinary edges and round/carve them, producing a visible facet at what should be a flat, continuous seam.

Solidify must be placed BEFORE Bevel when starting from an open/flat mesh (e.g. a plane). Bevel on an unsolidified single-face plane has no dihedral angle to act on and is effectively a no-op; Solidify must run first to give the mesh real 3D form.

Boolean before or after Bevel is a genuine strategic choice, not a correctness issue: Boolean-then-Bevel rounds the cut/hole rim too (more geometry); Bevel-then-Boolean leaves the cut sharp (less geometry). Choose based on whether the cut's edge should read as rounded or crisp.
expected_effects: Mirror+Subdivision: the selected order must have 0 non-manifold edges in the evaluated mesh and acceptable seam shape/highlight flow; topology-specific testing decides the order
Mirror+Bevel in the correct order (Bevel first): a flat, unrounded seam face at the mirror plane, with the two halves reading as one continuous surface
Solidify+Bevel in the correct order (Solidify first): the evaluated mesh's vertex/face count reflects real bevel geometry, not an unchanged flat shell
success_predicates: no evaluated vertices with visibly rounded/offset coordinates sitting exactly on the mirror plane when a flat seam was intended
failure_predicates: evaluated_mesh_health.non_manifold_edges > 0 after evaluating either tested Mirror/Subdivision order on the actual seam topology
Bevel modifier added but the evaluated mesh's vertex/face count is unchanged from before adding it (Bevel silently doing nothing, usually because it ran before Solidify on a flat shell)
recovery: reorder the modifier stack (Blender modifiers can be reordered without data loss -- this does not require rebuilding geometry) and re-check non_manifold_edges / vertex-face counts on the evaluated mesh

sources.description: This project's own live reproduction, session 2026-08-07 (knowledge-first foundation phase): built matched pairs of scratch objects (a cube with its inner face touching a mirror plane; a plane for Solidify+Bevel) with modifiers added in both orders, compared via evaluated_probe-style inspection (vertex/face/non-manifold counts, seam vertex positions).
sources.trust_tier: not applicable (first-party direct experiment, not an external source)

experiments.type: controlled, matched-pair (this project's own reproduction lab, not an external tutorial)
experiments.description: Mirror+Subdivision: Mirror->Subdivision gave 171v/176f/16 non-manifold edges; Subdivision->Mirror gave 196v/192f/0 non-manifold edges, with the evaluated seam empty of exactly-on-plane vertices in the working order and populated with rounded-looking coordinates in the broken order. Mirror+Bevel: Mirror->Bevel gave 68v/67f/12 non-manifold with bevelled coordinates at the seam; Bevel->Mirror gave 108v/107f/4 non-manifold with a flat unbevelled seam face. Solidify+Bevel: Solidify->Bevel gave 56v/54f; Bevel->Solidify gave 8v/6f, identical to an un-bevelled solidified plane (confirming the no-op). Boolean+Bevel: both orders gave 0 non-manifold edges but different face counts (248v/216f vs 120v/88f), confirming this pair is a style choice, not a correctness issue.
experiments.limitation: Tested on simple primitive shapes (cube, plane, cube+cylinder cutter), not yet on a real production prop combining these modifiers. The original Mirror+Subdivision result was topology-specific and must be read alongside the curved transfer experiment.

experiments.description: On an exact-seam half-cylinder in runs/2026-08-10_bevel-mirror-transfer/, Mirror->Subdivision and Subdivision->Mirror both evaluated to 482 vertices, 480 quad faces, and 0 non-manifold edges. The intentionally offset Mirror seam produced 12 non-manifold edges and a larger Merge Distance repaired it. Independent evaluation of the saved blend reproduced all outcomes.
experiments.limitation: Manifoldness and counts do not prove identical curvature or highlight flow. The two stack orders had slightly different signed volumes, and neither was judged with a controlled reflection render.

skill.status_note: Controlled matched-pair evidence exists for all four listed pairs, plus a cylindrical second-shape transfer for Mirror+Subdivision. The transfer disproved the universal version of the original order rule, so the skill now requires per-topology evaluation. Not yet RUNTIME_VALIDATED or BENCHMARK_SUPPORTED; no real prop has combined these modifiers and visual seam quality still needs controlled reflection evidence.
